deepseek.note: sweep: 12 suggested, 10 links answered; shortlist: 8 picked

profileDigest: Agentic HQ: a local-first personal agent homepage + "Second Brain" for one developer on Windows 11. Zero-dependency Node server (server.js on localhost) with lib/*.cjs helpers and tools/*.mjs CLIs; node --test suite; local git only. It launches and supervises coding-agent workers through a skills deck and Orca worktree orchestration, runs scheduled routines (Windows Task Scheduler + Claude Code scheduled tasks), meters each agent's usage limits, keeps an event inbox, an attention budget for ntfy phone pushes, and a ring of HTML report artifacts. Worker lanes: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, DeepSeek web (Orca browser), Kilo. Companions: Karakeep, changedetection.io, ntfy, promptfoo, QMD, Basic Memory, CASS session search. Micro apps: RUBRIC Recos, Paper Lantern, Agent HQ, AgentViz, Tidepool, Karakeep, Change Watch, ntfy, Prompt Evals, LearnHarness. Deck cards: api-hq-review, karakeep, change-watch, weekly-dev-health, session-lessons, gotcha-proposals, orbit-notes-release, fieldkit-drift-check, time-map, microapp-finder. Routines: Session lessons, morning action brief, inbox triage, Weekly routines check, docs watch, release radar, Dessa AI voice agent: release watc, Usage budget guard (24 runs today), PC sentinel (12 runs today) (+2 more).

findings.title: SkillTotal
findings.summary: SkillTotal, a static, no-LLM security scanner for npm/PyPI packages, MCP servers, agent skills and repos that reports findings with a file and line.
findings.whatsNew: v0.85.1 fixes a quadratic-time stall in the ST-CLIPPER rule; the ruleset and report schema are unchanged. It surfaced through the MCP registry listing.

fit.why: The owner installs third-party skills, plugins and MCP servers (QMD, Basic Memory, CASS, the radar's own finds), and HQ has no pre-install scan. It could also be run by hand on any radar 'adopt' candidate before install.
A deterministic scan result could become verified `dependencies` and risk evidence for radar items instead of 'not checked'.

reasoning.benefit: Turns the radar's unchecked supply-chain claims (install scripts, risky code) into evidence with a cited file and line, without running the code or spending LLM tokens.

risks.detail: Only 2 contributors in 90 days. A security tool with a small maintainer base is itself a trust point; pin the version and install with pipx, not the Claude plugin's auto-hook.
335 commits in 30 days and 98 releases mean fast churn in rules and output.

reasoning.counter: It has 2 contributors and 16 stars, and 0 issues ever filed means almost no outside validation. Its findings could be noisy enough that the owner ignores them.
reasoning.overlap: Nothing in HQ scans packages or skills. Grep of lib/tools found no scanner, only the usage-gate hook.

evidence.claim: Static scan; never runs code; no LLM; runs locally

evidence.how: README badge only; pyproject.toml not opened

evidence.claim: HQ has no existing package or skill scanner
evidence.how: Grep lib/tools/config for hook/scan/ignore-scripts: matches are unrelated (usage gate, radar)

steps: It fills a real HQ gap: no pre-install scan of skills, MCP servers or packages.
It is local, deterministic and token-free, which suits HQ's rules.
It fails the adopt bar on maintenance: only 2 contributors.
It is cheap to falsify on a throwaway worktree.
reasoning.maintenance: Last commit 2026-10-28; 335 commits in 30 days; 2 contributors in 90 days; 98 releases, latest v0.85.1; 0 issues (none filed).
reasoning.license: Apache-2.0: fine to use and vendor.
reasoning.dependencies: Python CLI through pipx. The README badge claims 0 runtime dependencies (pyproject.toml not opened to confirm). It is a scanner, not a service.
reasoning.falsify: Scanning 3 known-good HQ companions (e.g. the QMD and Basic Memory packages) and 1 sanitized bad sample gives high-severity false positives on the good ones, or misses the bad one.

plan: In a throwaway git worktree, install with `pipx install skilltotal==0.85.1` (user-scope, pinned, not the Claude plugin hook).
Run `skilltotal scan` on 3 known-good companions plus one sanitized bad sample, and save the reports to the scratchpad.
If the signal is good, add an optional evidence step in tools/ai-radar.mjs that shells out to skilltotal when it is on PATH, with fixture tests in new:test/radar-skilltotal.test.cjs.
findings.shortlistReason: Deterministic local scanner for MCP servers, agent skills, and packages fills a security-review gap in the skills deck without LLM dependency.

findings.title: Codex CLI v0.166.0

sources.signal: Memory v2 is on by default and the session picker filters across linked worktrees, matching your Orca worktree orchestration.

findings.summary: Codex CLI, the OpenAI terminal coding agent that HQ runs as a worker lane and meters for usage.
findings.whatsNew: v0.166.0 adds keyboard transcript selection and search, the GPT-6.1 Terra model, `codex queue --resume` and `codex doctor --network-only`. It also keeps approval settings and reasoning-token accounting across resume and fork, and fixes app-server startup and shutdown races.

fit.why: lib/usage-meters.cjs reads ~/.codex/sessions rollout-*.jsonl and parses rate_limits through codexMeterFromText/codexMeterFromRateLimits. A change in the rollout format would break the Codex meter.
`codex doctor --network-only` could be called as an optional probe, but HQ does not need it today.
Codex is scored as a profile (code 88). A new model in the catalog does not change routing.

reasoning.benefit: Keeping approval and permission settings across resume and fork, plus the app-server race fixes, make unattended Codex workers more reliable. HQ needs no code change.
reasoning.cost: usage: Codex (ChatGPT plan) tokens per worker run, unchanged

risks.detail: The 'reasoning-token accounting across resume/fork' change may alter what lands in rollout JSONL, which lib/usage-meters.cjs parses.

reasoning.counter: This is a routine update to a lane HQ already runs, not a new capability. The transcript and TUI features don't touch HQ, which drives Codex headless.
reasoning.overlap: Already covered by the Codex worker lane and the Codex meter in lib/usage-meters.cjs.

evidence.claim: Release adds queue --resume, doctor --network-only, and keeps settings and reasoning-token accounting on resume/fork
HQ parses Codex rollout JSONL for rate limits
The rollout rate_limits format is unchanged in 0.166.0

steps: Codex is an existing lane, so the question is regressions, not adoption.
HQ depends on the rollout JSONL format for the Codex meter.
The release notes show reliability fixes for resume/fork and the app-server, all positive.
No new HQ gap is filled.
Verdict: watch, with a quick meter check after updating.
reasoning.maintenance: Last commit 2026-10-29; 1279 commits in 30 days; 39 contributors in 90 days; 1257 releases; 25k open issues.
reasoning.dependencies: Standalone CLI binary (installer, npm -g or GitHub release), not imported by HQ.
reasoning.falsify: After updating, `node tools/usage-check.mjs --agent=codex --json` returns stale or unknown although a fresh Codex session exists. Then fixing the rollout parser becomes needed work.

plan: After updating Codex, run `node tools/usage-check.mjs --agent=codex --json` and check that the windows are fresh.
If parsing fails, add a 0.166 rollout fixture to the usage-meters tests and patch codexMeterFromText in lib/usage-meters.cjs.
findings.shortlistReason: Codex CLI is an active worker lane; v0.166.0 changes terminal transcript/search interactions the supervisor may depend on.

findings.title: anomalyco/opencode process-daemon-v0.4.0
findings.summary: OpenCode, an open-source coding agent; the pinned tag is an internal PTY process-daemon package, @opencode/pty 0.4.0 (protocol 7).
findings.whatsNew: The only release note is 'opencode-pty 0.4.0 (protocol 7) from packages/process-daemon, published to npm as @opencode/pty@0.4.0'. There is no changelog of behavior.

fit.why: OpenCode is an unmetered lane that is always allowed (usage-meters.cjs lines 152 and 159). HQ does not touch OpenCode's PTY layer.

reasoning.benefit: None to HQ directly. It is an internal component of OpenCode that its own CLI pulls in.

risks.detail: A protocol version bump could need matching OpenCode CLI and desktop versions, but that is OpenCode's concern, not HQ's.

reasoning.counter: HQ never talks to OpenCode's PTY daemon. Orca owns the terminals, so this package has no HQ integration point.
reasoning.overlap: Terminal and process supervision is handled by Orca (tools/orca-reap.mjs) and by HQ's own sentinel and restart guard (tools/hq-sentinel.mjs, lib/restart-guard.cjs).

evidence.claim: The release is only the internal PTY daemon package
HQ treats OpenCode as an unmetered, always-allowed lane
HQ has no direct PTY integration with OpenCode
evidence.how: Grep for 'pty' in lib/tools matched files about other topics; terminals are launched through Orca

steps: The release note describes an internal package bump only.
HQ does not integrate with OpenCode's daemon.
Process supervision is already covered by Orca and the sentinel.
reasoning.maintenance: Last commit 2026-10-29; 1865 commits in 30 days; 14 contributors; 889 releases.
reasoning.dependencies: npm package @opencode/pty. Its dependency count and install scripts were not checked; PTY packages usually ship native binaries.
reasoning.falsify: If HQ starts launching OpenCode itself outside Orca and needs resumable PTY sessions, re-review.

findings.shortlistReason: OpenCode is a worker lane; process-daemon/PTY release directly affects process supervision and resumable sessions.
